I1.quote: The hydrogen storage capacity of the samples was measured by the gravimetric method at 77 K (ISOSORP-HyGrA, Waters Corporation, Milford, MA, USA).

I2.quote: Porous carbon fiber (PCF) and activated porous carbon fiber (APCF) were derived by carbonization and chemical activation after selectively removing polyvinyl alcohol from a bi-component fiber composed of polyvinyl alcohol and polyacrylonitrile (PAN).

I3.quote: CF, ACF, PCF_H 0.3, and APCF_H 0.3, with surface areas of 11, 316, 889, and 3058 m2 g−1 respectively, have hydrogen storage capacities of 0.07, 1.35, 2.87, and 5.14 wt%, respectively, at 77 K and 10 MPa.

I4.quote: APCF_H 0.3 exhibits an ultra-high BET surface area of 3058 m2 g−1 and a pore volume of 1.55 cm3 g−1 (Figure 4).

I5.quote: In this study, highly porous carbon fiber was prepared for hydrogen storage.

notes: Original research article (Nanomaterials 2021, 11, 1830); record is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF; no statement that the H2 uptake values were published before.
